To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ceramic protonic conductor, SrCe0.9Yb0.1O3−α, is a good material for the electrochemical hydrogen extraction from the pyrolysized gases of CO + H20 mixture, ethane and steam.

we have found that SrCe0.9Yb0.1O3-α ceramic has protonic and electronic conductivity in hydrogen gas and the electronic conductivity increases in oxygen gas, and we have successfully applied this ceramic as a diaphragm to the hydrogen extraction and the electrolysis of steam.

the protonic conductivity of SrCe0,95Yb0,05O3−a ceramic is 2 orders of magntiude higher than electronic conductivity and that hydrogen gas can be extracted from the pyrolysized gas of CO +H2O mixture, methane or steam by using SrCeO3-based protonic conductor as a solid electrolytic diaphragm.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new protonic conductors and its application to hydrogen gas extraction.
the development of a new type of proton conductor, which is a perovskite type of oxide, Sr(Ce1−yZry)O3−δ.

the development of a new type of hydrogen extractor, which can extract pure hydrogen gas from various hydrogen sources, such as steam, pyrolysis of hydrocarbon, and hydrolysis of hydrides, by using a high temperature protonic conductor.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a new protonic conductor, SrCeO3, has been developed and the hydrogen extractor using this material has been demonstrated.

the protonic conductivity of SrCe0,95Yb0,05O3−a ceramic is high enough to be used as a solid electrolytes in fuel cell and hydrogen extraction devices, and that the hydrogen extraction device is a very promising method to extract hydrogen from various hydrocarbon sources.
the protonic conductor based SrCeO3 can be applied to a high temperature type hydrogen extractor.

the high temperature protonic conductor is a useful material for the hydrogen extraction from various sources.

a high temperature type hydrogen extractor has been successfully developed.

we have successfully extracted hydrogen from a variety of hydrocarbon sources using a protonic conductor as a diaphragm.
the proton conductor can extract hydrogen from a mixture of hydrogen and oxygen, or hydrogen and carbon, and can be used as a solid electrolytic diaphragm for a fuel cell.
